session_summary: v3: fixed the 'stuck in dispatching' live-update bug (code-analyst root-caused: chokidar native fs-events unreliable for container-written logs on Windows/WSL mounts → switched to poll-cadence re-tail), then built two researched features — a journal-driven scrum-master hub monitor (project-planner designed docs/scrum-master-monitor-design.md) and pod distinction (docs/pod-distinction-design.md: pod = /workspace mount source via cached docker inspect, scope-to-self default + --all-pods/--pod, per-pod color + compound-parent clusters + legend). 3 commits (8ef6ca1, 7e536c5, 7782aa7) pushed; PR #1 updated. 89/89 tests; all QA gates green. bd stats: 41 total / 41 closed / 0 open.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Pinpointed a subtle live-update bug (event-driven chokidar vs needed poll-tail) with exact file:line evidence and ruled out the orchestrator's poll-reset hypothesis — gave the scrum-master a directly-decomposable fix with no guesswork.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: Again hit the turn budget before a [DONE] line on one run though the analysis file was written; orchestrator verified via the artifact.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Strong on focused frontend slices (per-pod hue + legend) and even diagnosed that prior compound-parent scaffolding was unwired and completed it.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: A combined 'pod color + legend + compound clusters + multi-hub' task TIMED OUT on the 10-minute execution wall while over-thinking (wrote nothing). Splitting it into two smaller tasks (color+legend, then clustering) both completed fine. Lesson: large multi-concern frontend tasks should be pre-split; the wall is ~10 min regardless of max_turns.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Handled interdependent backend slices (journal parser+watcher, reconciler hub+state+cli, pod scoping across 4 files) coherently with tests green each time; reused the bug-fix's poll-tail mechanism for the journal so the hub didn't inherit the same lag.

overall_notes: Two transient platform failures (not task design) the orchestrator had to recognize and retry cleanly: a 429 'Server is temporarily limiting requests (not your usage limit)' that killed a dispatch instantly (clean retry succeeded), and a 10-minute execution-wall TIMEOUT on an over-scoped ui-designer task (fixed by splitting). Recurring '.gitconfig: Device or resource busy' stderr warnings on parallel container starts appear harmless. Pattern that worked well this session: code-analyst/project-planner research FIRST for any non-trivial bug or feature (the dispatching bug and both features each began with a Tier-2 research pass that produced an anchored, decomposable plan), then fullstack-dev/ui-designer implement small validated slices. Key engineering lesson worth propagating: on Windows/WSL Docker bind-mounts, native fs-watch (chokidar) is unreliable for actively-growing container-written files — prefer an interval offset-tail (usePolling) over awaitWriteFinish/event-only watching. Tooling unchanged (alexandria reachable; beads shared-server fine).
